documents.unit: Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (CETL)
documents.title: AI Guidelines (archived copy)
documents.summary: A teaching-center page that shares Idaho statewide principles for generative AI, advises instructors to decide and explain their own AI rules in the syllabus, lists possible student and instructor uses, and offers three syllabus templates. It takes no institutional stance and is advisory.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own: "Our goal is ... not to advocate for or against your use or your students use of such tools". It tells instructors "Your Decisions" (not use / use) and offers three syllabus examples from "No AI Allowed" to "Unconditional AI Allowed", so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The page frames CETL's role as informing faculty practice and policy ('seeks to inform faculty instructional practices and policies'), a statement of purpose and scope rather than a rule, so P56 with informs.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source's opening sentence says CETL 'seeks to inform faculty instructional practices and policies', a statement of the center's purpose. Coder A coded the page-goal sentence a few lines later but not this one. Kept as a framing statement (P56, informs).
units.anchor: seeks to inform faculty instructional practices and policies

units.why: The center states it will "offer workshops and consultations on AI’s uses and limitations for faculty", which is faculty support for learning about AI, so P63.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed only on unit_stance (A neutral, B encourage); final unit_stance neutral. The passage describes or lists something and takes no position on AI use, so the neutral unit_stance is kept; the other codes follow the source wording.
units.anchor: offer workshops and consultations on AI’s uses and limitations for faculty

units.why: CETL says it takes part in "SBoE and multi-institutional working groups", an engagement with peers and the state board, so P88 (coalitions) rather than P63.
units.resolution_why: Coder A put the working-group sentence in general, coder B in over-time. It states a current affiliation ('We are involved in SBoE and multi-institutional working groups'), not a review cycle or evidence, so general.
units.anchor: involved in SBoE and multi-institutional working groups to advance our knowledge

units.why: CETL "sponsor[s] a cross-disciplinary AI faculty group", a faculty community for learning about AI, which is P63.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: before-course; coder B: over-time. The faculty group is faculty support set up for instructors ('sponsor a cross-disciplinary AI faculty group'); 'now in its second year' only dates it. It does not describe review or revision, so before-course, as for the workshops unit.
units.anchor: sponsor a cross-disciplinary AI faculty group, now in its second year

units.why: The page states its purpose and scope ("summarize, share, and invite information and recommendations on ... best practices"), a framing statement, so P56; it is not itself a rule.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says 'The goal of this webpage is to summarize, share, and invite information and recommendations ... best practices'. It is a purpose statement for the page, so kept as P56 informs.
units.anchor: summarize, share, and invite information and recommendations on existing and emerging best practices for AI
units.fit_note: Page purpose statement rather than an institution-wide framework with principles.

units.why: It says who made the principles and when ("created by members of the Idaho Statewide AI Alliance in January 2024"), so P84 describes how the guidance was made.

units.anchor: focus on human judgment, empathy, and ethical discernment when harnessing generative AI

units.why: The principles are non-binding ("not hard and fast rules") but users are told it is "a good idea" to keep them in mind, a recommendation attached to the framework, so P56 with should.
units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed (A neutral, B encourage). The sentence says the principles are 'not hard and fast rules' and it is 'a good idea to review them'. That recommends reading the principles, not AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: not hard and fast rules, it is a good idea to review them
units.fit_note: States that the framework is advisory, not binding.

units.why: The first listed principle ("People come first.") is a statement of values inside the shared framework, so P56.
units.anchor: People come first.

units.resolution_why: Coder A: should, coder B: informs. The source says 'An inquiry mindset will foster a culture of continuous learning about AI', a statement of what a mindset does, with no duty or recommendation to act. So informs, neutral. P102 stays the nearest type (fit_note kept).
units.anchor: An inquiry mindset will foster a culture of continuous learning about AI.
units.fit_note: Framed as a principle, not a stated duty. / Framed as a cultural principle ('inquiry mindset') rather than a duty to follow guidance.

units.why: "Learners need equitable access to generative AI" is an equity and access principle, matching P51.
units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed (A neutral, B encourage). 'Learners need equitable access to generative AI' supports access to AI, so encourage. Type, actor and modality agreed.
units.anchor: Learners need equitable access to generative AI.
units.fit_note: Stated as a principle about learner access, not as an alternative or accommodation in a course.

units.why: This principle ("Responsive, engaged teaching matters more than ever") is a value statement in the framework, so P56.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P56; coder B: UNCOVERED. The sentence 'Responsive, engaged teaching matters more than ever' is one of the six listed shared principles; both coders put 'People come first' in P56. Same list, same kind of statement, so P56.

documents.title: Syllabus Language for AI
documents.summary: A knowledge-base article from the Center for Teaching & Learning with three ready-to-paste syllabus statements: AI prohibited, AI only with prior instructor permission, and AI allowed with citation and a short note. Each ties violations to the Student Code of Conduct.
documents.stance_why: The article offers three options and says "please choose one or specify your own", so the university sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors; the options ("AI Use Prohibited", "AI with Prior Permission", "AI with Acknowledgement") are tiers.

units.why: The template tells instructors 'please choose one or specify your own' of the options, so the instructor sets the AI rule, P04. The named tiers are coded in the separate Option 1 label unit (P05).
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P05, course-start, may; coder B: P04, before-course, should. The text '(please choose one or specify your own)' is an instruction to the instructor to pick a rule or write one, which is P04; the three named options are coded under P05 in B's separate label unit. 'please choose' is a request, so should; the choice is course design, so before-course.
units.anchor: (please choose one or specify your own)
units.fit_note: Also frames the offered options as named tiers (P05); the tiers are coded in their own unit.

units.why: Three labelled options (prohibited, prior permission, acknowledgement) form named tiers of AI use: P05.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The labels 'OPTION 1) AI Use Prohibited', 'AI with Prior Permission', 'AI with Acknowledgement' are three named tiers of AI use. Kept as P05 for the tiers, which coder A folded into the 'choose one' unit. Phase course-start because the options are syllabus language.
units.anchor: OPTION 1) AI Use Prohibited

units.why: The boilerplate says it "is important to clarify how they may or may not be used in this course", the aim of stating an AI rule in the syllabus, P09.
units.resolution_why: Modality differed (A informs, B should). The boilerplate says 'it is important to clarify how they may or may not be used in this course'. It is written in the syllabus voice as the reason for the policy, not as an order to anyone, so informs.
units.anchor: important to clarify how they may or may not be used in this course
units.fit_note: Appears in all three options; coded once.

units.why: The text defines scope by listing "ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity, Grammarly, image generators, and automated coding/writing assistants", a definition of AI tools covered, P61.
units.resolution_why: Actor differed (A all, B student). The listed tools define the scope of all three options, so all.
units.anchor: including but not limited to ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity, Grammarly, image generators, and automated coding/writing assistants
units.fit_note: Appears in all three options; coded once. Includes Grammarly and coding assistants.

units.why: Option 1 says AI tools "[are] not permitted in this course", a default ban, P01.
units.anchor: assistants—is not permitted in this course

units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed (A prohibit, B neutral). In Option 1 the sentence says unauthorized AI use 'is considered a form of unauthorized assistance', which supports the ban, so prohibit.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of AI tools is considered a form of unauthorized assistance

units.why: Option 1 grounds the ban in skill-building: the course "build[s] foundational skills ... that require your direct engagement", so P41.
units.resolution_why: Phase and unit stance differed (A course-start/prohibit, B general/neutral). 'This course is intentionally designed to build foundational skills' is a rationale, so general and neutral.
units.anchor: intentionally designed to build foundational skills

units.why: It says using AI "to generate or revise work may hinder the achievement of these objectives", the practice-shortcut rationale, P41.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The next sentence says 'Using AI tools to generate or revise work may hinder the achievement of these objectives', a second part of the rationale. Kept as P41, general, neutral, matching the previous unit.
units.anchor: Using AI tools to generate or revise work may hinder the achievement of these objectives

units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed (A permit, B restrict). The ban holds 'unless explicitly allowed by the instructor for a specific assignment', i.e. banned unless permitted, which is restrict.

units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source says AI tools 'may be used in this course only with prior instructor permission', the default rule of Option 2. Coder A did not code this sentence. B coded it P06, but the sentence states the default (banned without permission) rather than what applies when a syllabus is silent, which is the next sentence, so P01.
units.anchor: only with prior instructor permission

units.why: Option 2 sets the rule when no permission is given: "all assignments must be completed independently and without assistance from automated tools", a fallback ban, P06.
units.resolution_why: Policy type differed (A P06, B P01). The source says 'Unless permission is explicitly granted, all assignments must be completed independently and without assistance from automated tools', which matches the P06 definition ('unless explicitly allowed, AI is prohibited'), so P06.
units.anchor: Unless permission is explicitly granted, all assignments must be completed independently

units.why: Option 2 requires students to "email a description of your AI request to your instructor" before the work, asking first, P10.
units.resolution_why: Phase differed (A before-course, B during-work). Students must email the request 'prior to completing your assignment', so the step happens as they start the work, during-work.
units.anchor: Email a description of your AI request to your instructor
units.fit_note: Mandatory pre-approval request, stronger than 'ask when unsure'.

units.why: If permission is given, students "must ... cite any AI-generated material" in a recognized format, a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: cite any AI-generated material using a clear attribution and appropriate citation format

units.why: Students must "include a brief (2-3 sentence) note explaining how the tool was used, including the prompt or settings", which names prompt and settings details, P25.
units.anchor: include a brief (2–3 sentence) note explaining how the tool was used
units.fit_note: Also requires a brief note on how the tool was used, a reflection-like statement.

units.why: "Undisclosed use of AI tools will be considered a violation of academic integrity", so failure to disclose is itself the violation, P28.
units.resolution_why: Modality and unit stance differed (A must/restrict, B informs/prohibit). 'Unauthorized or undisclosed use of AI tools will be considered a violation of academic integrity' states a consequence, so informs. AI is allowed once documented and permitted, so the position is restrict.
units.anchor: Unauthorized or undisclosed use of AI tools will be considered a violation of academic integrity
units.fit_note: Also treats unauthorized use as a violation and says grade may be affected (not a fixed penalty).

units.why: 'This practice helps you reflect on your learning process and ensures transparency': the reason given for documenting AI use, P66.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: UNCOVERED; coder B: P66. The source says 'This practice helps you reflect on your learning process and ensures transparency'. P66's definition covers giving students the reasons behind AI rules, so it fits and no new type is needed. It is addressed to students as part of the syllabus, so course-start.
units.anchor: ensures transparency in your academic work
units.fit_note: Gives the rationale for a disclosure rule (reflection and transparency) rather than the rule. Coder A coded this UNCOVERED ('Rationale for the disclosure requirement: reflection and transparency').

units.why: Students unsure how to document AI use are told to "reach out or visit the University of Idaho Writing Center", a pointer to human support, P72.
units.anchor: University of Idaho Writing Center

units.why: Option 3 allows AI tools "if that use is properly documented and cited", a permit-with-conditions default, P02.
units.anchor: may be used in this course if that use is properly documented and cited

documents.title: Student Conduct
documents.summary: The Dean of Students conduct page describes the Student Code of Conduct process. AI appears only twice: prohibited AI tools count as academic dishonesty, and students are told to read each syllabus because instructors set different AI limits.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI stance of its own; it lists "reliance on prohibited technological assistance/artificial intelligence tools" as dishonesty and says "each instructor may have different limits or expectations of use", so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: Under prohibited behavior in academic dishonesty, the Code lists "reliance on prohibited technological assistance/artificial intelligence tools", classing prohibited AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.resolution_why: Unit stance differed (A prohibit, B restrict). The Code lists only 'reliance on prohibited technological assistance/artificial intelligence tools', so AI is misconduct only where it is prohibited; restrict.
units.anchor: reliance on prohibited technological assistance/artificial intelligence tools

units.why: The page says "individual instructors may establish additional academic integrity expectations for their courses", leaving AI limits to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: individual instructors may establish additional academic integrity expectations for their courses
units.fit_note: Stated for academic integrity expectations in general; AI is covered by implication and in the later AI line. / Stated for academic integrity expectations generally, not AI specifically.

units.why: Students are told to review instructor expectations in syllabi 'carefully': P78.
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored on 'can vary based on subject matter and teaching style', coder B on 'be sure to review them carefully'. Same sentence, same codes; B's anchor carries the duty.
units.anchor: be sure to review them carefully
units.fit_note: Applies to academic integrity expectations generally, not AI only. / Not AI-specific.

units.why: Students are told "each instructor may have different limits or expectations of use. Read your course syllabus carefully!", a duty to find and follow each course's AI rules, P78.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P78, should; coder B: P11, informs. The sentence 'each instructor may have different limits or expectations of use' says one instructor's AI rule does not carry over to another course, which is P11 and a statement of fact. The duty to read the syllabus is in the next sentence, coded P78 as its own unit.
units.anchor: each instructor may have different limits or expectations of use

units.why: 'Read your course syllabus carefully!' tells students to find each course's AI rules: P78.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. 'Read your course syllabus carefully!' is a separate instruction to students. Coder A merged it into the previous unit. Kept as P78.
units.anchor: Read your course syllabus carefully!
